chapter_mission: Veranthos from orbit, descent, and the first night at the valley's edge. The ring structure delivers escalating wrongness. The city has not been destroyed — it has drifted. The Scar is visible in the valley from the ridgeline. Torin stands at the camp edge with the expression of a man coming home. Per W2 Option α (conditional), a flexibility slot sits in s2: Ben glimpses Veraine at distance on a ridgeline opposite as the group descends through the evacuation zone — a failed-interception beat preserved as pacing-refresh capacity. If α is not drafted, the slot converts to a Veraine ledger entry Ben reads in camp at s3 (an entry on a midpoint-era site, her reading of the technique-lineage fragment). Either way, the chapter carries one further piece of Veraine's working mind between the Ch 19 annotation and the Ch 22 array-component encounter.
chapter_turn: Everything converges tomorrow. The book's geography and the book's characters line up on the same clock. Ben does not yet know the content of what is coming; he knows the shape of it, and Torin's silhouette against the stars announces it without a word. PP18 (Veraine as architect of the ritual site's exact geography) pays silently — Ben's descent confirms that everything he has been tracking about the array-dependency fact is true at the scale of the place itself. PP25 (the wound as lived galactic texture, not cosmic concept) pays in Desh's grief-without-an-object landing in the evacuation-zone city.

scene_plan.purpose: Orbit over Veranthos. Blue-green oceans, temperate forests, beautiful. Scan data contradicts the beauty — weather patterns not following rotation, vegetation defying sunlight, ocean currents reversed. The seal boundary visible in Force perception as a membrane; beyond it the wound, gravitational. Desh: 'Her ship is on the surface. Valley coordinates. She's already there.' Ben overlays the array-dependency picture the group assembled at Ch 14 against the geography now under them — every topographic feature slots. The place is the apparatus. H18 and H19 resolve. PP18 begins its silent payoff.

Descent through the ring structure. Ring 4: seal boundary — Ben crosses it and the Force drops away entirely, not thinned but gone. Ring 3: evacuation zone — doors standing open, vehicles pointed away from the valley, a thousand years of overgrowth. Ring 2: the city — homes, shops, a school, a child's toy on a step, vines climbing and reversing, flowers blooming on shadow faces. Desh's grief-without-an-object lands without mysticism (PP25 pays). The ridgeline opens on the valley. The Scar — a three-meter vertical distortion where the Force was torn — is visible below. Ben stops walking. Per W2 Option α (conditional flexibility slot, default PLANTED AS CAPACITY not executed unless drafting calls for a villain-refresh beat): in the evacuation-zone passage, Ben may glimpse Veraine at distance on an opposing ridge — a figure standing still, watching the group descend, too far to pursue, gone before the binoculars focus. No exchange. No taunt. The beat is a sighting and a registration: she is already here, she has allowed herself to be seen, she did not stay. If α is not executed, the chapter passes through s2 without this beat and the slot converts to β at s3 (see s3 purpose).

Camp at the valley's edge. Night. The Scar visible against the stars — a line of absence outlined by light. Torin stands at the camp perimeter and has not looked away from the valley since they arrived. His Force presence has softened. He looks younger. More alive. More dangerous. Ben watches from the tent and understands: tomorrow. H20 plants. Per W2 Option α β-fallback (default path if α not executed in s2): at the edge of the scene Ben sits with his datapad and reads a second Veraine ledger entry — pulled during the outpost archive sync earlier, surfaced now as his attention returns to it. The entry is her working notes on a midpoint-era site (implied Kolven, unnamed), her reading of the technique-lineage fragment Ben has been chasing since Ch 11. Short. Precise. The working mind in its native register. She reaches a conclusion Ben reaches from the opposite direction and identifies a structural feature of Gavran's original containment work that Gavran himself missed. The intellectual sharpness is the threat. (If α was executed in s2, the ledger beat shortens to a one-paragraph coda — Ben reading the same entry as a reflexive return to her voice after seeing her in the flesh.)

relationship_turns.to: present place — the world Ben has been navigating toward for three acts exists under his boots. Its beauty is a symptom. Its silence is architecture. His Force-sense is gone inside the seal boundary. He will operate without it for the rest of the book
already gone — Torin at the camp edge is not with them anymore, and no one pretends he is. The group's composure is performance for Ben's benefit; they are all watching what he will do

grief-without-an-object — the non-Force-sensitive experience of full unweaving lands in s2. The wound affects everyone; the book's thematic claim about the Weave mattering to non-Force-users becomes physical here

present-and-unreachable — per W2 evidence-of-passage beat 3: whether α (glimpsed at distance, s2) or β (second ledger entry, s3), Ben now registers Veraine as an active intelligence operating in the same space at the same time. Her certainty is not deterred by his proximity. The evidence beat refreshes the audience-relationship without requiring a direct scene

exit_vector: Camp silent on the ridge. Torin's silhouette against the line of the Scar. Veraine already somewhere in the valley. Desh in the tent with his instruments, Sera not watching Torin watch, Kael awake but motionless. The clock is at hours and the chapter closes with Ben understanding that the second plot point is not coming — it is here.
notes: Use the full Veranthos world-building from extended_metadata.world_building: ring structure, the city's drift (vines reversing, flowers on shadow faces, horizontal tree splits, no birds), the Scar as heat shimmer without heat, barely visible straight on, unmistakable at an angle. Ben's Force-sense going from present to absent at Ring 4's boundary is a phenomenological milestone — use the full_de_structuring sensory vocabulary, but rotate vocabulary families (force_mechanics.vocabulary_variation) away from 'handrail gone' — he has used that language. Desh's grief-without-an-object in s2 must land without mysticism; force_mechanics.sensory_vocabulary.full_de_structuring.non_force_sensitive specifies the register — a sadness about nothing that does not lift until leaving the zone. The Scar in s2 close is the reader's first direct look at the thing the book has been describing indirectly since Ch1. It must feel like sight, not concept. Per W2 Option α/β: the conditional slot is the chapter's flexibility pressure-valve. Default drafting assumption is β (the second ledger entry at s3) since evidence-of-presence has been carrying the villain-refresh load well since Ch 16-19; α is available if, at drafting, the chapter reads as needing a direct villain-refresh beat between the Ch 16 meeting and the Ch 25 climactic confrontation. The slot is designed so that neither choice alters the chapter's exit vector or word target. Voice: Zahn-procedural in s1; permit one Stover-dense beat for Ben's step through the seal boundary and one for the Scar reveal; Zahn-tight for s3. Veraine's ledger voice (if β executed) is continuous with Ch 17 and Ch 19 — precise, certain, minimal affect, unaddressed. ANTI-PATTERNS: (a) do not describe the ruined city as a disaster zone — the point is that it is intact and still wrong; (b) do not have Torin speak in s3 — his silhouette is the line; (c) no combat or confrontation this chapter — this is the chapter of the held breath; (d) per W2 Option α anti-pattern, if α is executed, Ben does not chase; no attempted interception. The beat is a sighting, a frozen second, an absence where the figure was; (e) per W2 anti-pattern, Veraine's ledger register does not warm or sharpen across the evidence beats — the working mind is consistent; (f) per D5, SP5 remains present here as Desh's operational instruments and grief-beat are load-bearing, but the chapter does not lean on a standalone Desh arc — his presence is supporting thematic weight.
